title: Smoky Maple-Soy Chicken Tenderloins with Butternut Squash, Corn and Black Beans
summary: Glazed chicken tenderloins served over a smoky skillet of butternut squash, corn and black beans.
sourceNote: A quick, high-protein dinner built around chicken tenderloins, pre-cut butternut squash and pantry-friendly vegetables without relying on potatoes or rice.

steps.text: In a small bowl, combine 1 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce, 2 tsp maple syrup, 1 tsp olive oil, 1/2 tsp smoked paprika and 1/4 tsp ground ginger.
Pat 1 lb chicken tenderloins dry and season them with black pepper. Do not add salt; the soy sauce supplies the seasoning.
Heat 1 tsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken tenderloins in a single layer and cook for 3 to 4 minutes. Work in two batches if needed to avoid crowding.
Turn the chicken tenderloins and cook for another 2 to 3 minutes.
Reduce the heat to medium. Pour the maple-soy glaze over the chicken and turn the tenderloins through it for 30 to 60 seconds, until the glaze thickens and the chicken reaches 165 F.

Transfer the chicken to a plate and let it rest for at least 5 minutes. While it rests, place 12 oz pre-cubed butternut squash and 1 tbsp water in a covered microwave-safe bowl; microwave for 4 to 5 minutes, until barely fork-tender NCC.
Drain the butternut squash well. Add up to 2 tbsp water to the skillet and scrape up the browned glaze.
Add the remaining 2 tsp olive oil and the par-cooked butternut squash. Cook over medium-high heat for 4 to 5 minutes, until browned in spots.
Add 1.5 cups frozen corn, the remaining 1/2 tsp smoked paprika, 1/4 tsp ground cumin, salt and black pepper. Cook for 4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the corn is hot.
Add 1/2 of a 15-oz can of rinsed and drained black beans. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, then taste and adjust the salt and pepper.
Divide the butternut squash, corn and black bean mixture between two plates and top with the glazed chicken tenderloins.
